answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when independently audited work is fraudulent or repeatedly duplicated. Creating a thousand fake identities does not multiply influence: each one needs its own capital at risk, and coordinated fakes can lose it all. A copper deposit, saffron-tagged audit record, and velvet reward for verified work can make the rule legible without treating identity clues as proof.
